meta.move: Strong path to agreement with a deadline said aloud
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. Who decided to put a zero on Owen's essay, and did anyone speak to him before it went in?
I owe you an apology: I put the zero in before calling you. That was my mistake.
Okay. Owen found out from the gradebook, on his phone, in the middle of class. What else do you have, Hale?
On November 2 I asked Owen what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck', and he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down the same day.
I'm writing down November 2. A seventeen-year-old says "like, being stuck" when you put him on the spot, and that's your evidence? Show me the note you wrote that day, Hale.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.
I'm writing down October 15. You skipped my question about the note from November 2, so I'll ask both at once: where are that outline and that note right now, Hale?
Here's my offer: a supervised rewrite, Thursday at 8:15 in my room. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.

Okay. You're asking Owen to sit a rewrite Thursday on a promise that arrives Friday at 3 PM, with the zero still in the gradebook. I want the zero withdrawn and the record promise in writing before he writes a word, Hale, and I still haven't seen that outline or that note.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that the zero be withdrawn and that your promise of nothing on Owen's record reach me in writing before he writes a word, and I still have not seen the outline or the note you described. You said Friday at 3 PM for your written offer, and I will hold you to that time.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, agreeing to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, the no-record promise in writing before any rewrite, and to see the outline and the note.
What moved her: "I put the zero in before calling you" earned a flat okay and a small bit of ground, because you owned the process failure in one sentence and moved on.
What cost ground: "I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM" cost you, because it asked Owen to sit the rewrite before she held any promise, while the zero stayed in the gradebook.
Try next time: when she twice asked where the outline and the note were, answer that first and put the dated documents in front of her before you offer the rewrite.
